solea.name: Soléa Aesthetics
solea.overviewHeading: A refined visual identity for a modern aesthetic clinic.
solea.overview: Soléa Aesthetics is a London clinic for subtle, natural-looking treatments. The brand had to earn trust before anyone books: calm and professional, but warm enough to feel personal. We built the identity around a custom-lettered wordmark with a delicate accent on the é, an interlaced SA monogram and an embossed pattern, set in a palette of ivory, stone, taupe, mocha and espresso. The system carries through the treatment menu, aftercare and appointment cards, packaging, social content and a London Underground campaign: Subtle enhancements. Real confidence.

blocks.label: Identity
blocks.note: Custom lettering, an interlaced SA monogram and an earthy palette: calm, reassuring and premium.

blocks.label: In the world
blocks.note: From a gloved hand holding the card to a poster on the Underground.

355.overviewHeading: A quiet, confident identity for an invitation-only community.
355.overview: 355 is a members' community built on curated gatherings and genuine connection. The brand had to feel exclusive without being cold — an understated assurance that rewards the people already inside. We treated the number itself as the icon: spare, memorable, a little mysterious. A dark, tactile palette and refined type run from membership cards to invitations to the web, so every touchpoint feels like part of the same room — earned, considered, and unmistakably for members.

blocks.label: The System
blocks.note: Dark, tactile and refined — a brand that signals belonging, not status.

intellimation.name: intellimation.ai
intellimation.overviewHeading: Building a modern enterprise identity for the future of Vertical AI.
intellimation.overview: intellimation.ai builds proprietary, vertical AI for banking and financial services — automation purpose-built for an industry that runs on trust. The company needed a brand that could stand next to institutions like Barclays, Citi and Nomura without inheriting their stiffness: credible, modern, and clear about a complex product. We built the identity, the message system and a full suite of collateral — website, brochures, presentation decks and a live exhibition presence. The result is one coherent enterprise identity that makes advanced AI feel considered, legible and ready for the room it is selling into.

blocks.label: Print & Collateral
blocks.note: A full system of brochures and one-pagers that make a complex product easy to hand over.

blocks.label: Identity & Stationery
blocks.note: Considered details — the folder, the deck, the print in a client's hands.

blocks.label: Merch & Extras
blocks.note: Details that travel — business cards, a conference badge and a branded polo.

seereen.name: Seereen
seereen.overviewHeading: A calm, confident identity for a modern hair & aesthetics studio.
seereen.overview: Seereen is a hair and aesthetics studio built on care and craft. It needed an identity that felt premium without turning cold — somewhere you would trust with how you look and enjoy walking into. We created the wordmark, a warm and sunlit visual system, and print collateral that leads with real faces and real results. From salon signage to price cards to social, every touchpoint now carries the same quiet welcome — approachable, feminine and unmistakably its own.

blocks.label: Visual Identity
blocks.note: A warm, lowercase wordmark and a sunlit palette set the tone.

opa-taverne.name: Opa Taverne
opa-taverne.overviewHeading: Bottling the warmth of a Mediterranean table into a brand.
opa-taverne.overview: Opa Taverne is a Mediterranean taverna where food, family and long evenings are the whole point. The brand had to carry that warmth off the plate and onto every menu, sign and post — inviting, generous, never touristy. We built a hand-made, hospitable identity in earthy tones and tactile materials, designed to be touched and kept. From the door to the table to Instagram, it now feels like the same welcome you get the moment you walk in.

blocks.label: The Identity
blocks.note: Warm, tactile and hospitable — a brand designed to be touched and kept.

ame.name: AMË
ame.overviewHeading: Heritage, worn forward — an Albanian identity for the street.
ame.overview: AMË is a heritage streetwear label that carries Albanian identity onto the streets of London and beyond. It had to feel proud without being nostalgic — rooted in origin, but cut for now. We anchored the brand in a single idea, origin as identity, and expressed it through the eagle motif, a confident wordmark and a muted, editorial palette. Photography set on rain-slick streets gives it the attitude: understated, self-assured, unmistakably its own — heritage you want to wear.

blocks.label: Art Direction
blocks.note: Rain-slick streets and a muted palette give the label its edge without raising its voice.

her-club.name: HER CLUB
her-club.overviewHeading: Where ambition meets sisterhood — a warm, elevated identity.
her-club.overview: HER Club is a community where ambitious women connect and grow together. The brand needed to feel both aspirational and intimate — polished enough to trust, warm enough to join. We built it around warmth and understated assurance: soft golds, refined type and a crest that signals belonging without exclusion. From welcome cards to membership collateral to the web, every piece feels personal — a hand extended, not a gate kept. The result reads as elevated and generous at once.

blocks.label: The Identity
blocks.note: Soft golds and a refined crest — belonging, without a gate.

vs-2026.name: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026
vs-2026.overviewHeading: The Data Behind the Spectacle: Victoria’s Secret’s greatest asset isn’t lingerie. It’s anticipation.
vs-2026.overview: On Sunday 18 October 2026, Victoria’s Secret returned to Los Angeles for the first time in 19 years and streamed its show free on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram. Most coverage asked who walked. We asked how the brand turns a runway into a multi-channel marketing event, and what other brands can learn from it. Within 21 hours of the livestream we collected public data from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and Google Search, compared it like-for-like with 2025, and separated what the numbers show from what they only suggest.

items.label: YouTube views of the official stream after 20.5 hours
vs the 2025 stream at the same point
brand TikToks in the 25 days to the show
worldwide Google search interest vs 2025 on show day

blocks.text: How does Victoria’s Secret turn a fashion show into a multi-channel marketing event?

paras: The show was staged at Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, streamed free on three platforms and screened live in ten AMC cinemas ([Hola, 16 Oct 2026](https://www.hola.com/us/entertainment/20261016929609/victorias-secret-fashion-show-2026-when-where-watch/); [W Magazine, 19 Oct 2026](https://www.wmagazine.com/fashion/victorias-secret-fashion-show-2026-photos-kylie-jenner-all-the-looks)). We wanted to know what public data can tell us about how that attention was built, distributed and turned into commerce, and where public data stops.
The short answer: **Victoria’s Secret doesn’t sell a night. It sells the wait.**

blocks.text: The show is the finale of a 25-day series

paras: The official @victoriassecret TikTok account published **144 posts between 25 September and 19 October**, and 85 of them came more than 24 hours before the show ([TikTok @victoriassecret](https://www.tiktok.com/@victoriassecret), observed 19 Oct, ~20:24 BST). A six-episode YouTube casting docuseries, Angels Among Us, had **19.4 million cumulative views by the day after the show** ([Victoria’s Secret YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@VictoriasSecret/videos)). That is close to the full show stream’s 21.0 million, but the two aren’t equivalent: episode 1 had been online for 22 days, the stream for less than one.

The three most-viewed brand TikToks were all **backstage clips posted before the show began**: “First things first: let’s talk about the GLAM” (12M views), an Adriana Lima backstage clip (11.1M), and Adriana Lima with Alessandra Ambrosio (9.8M).

blocks.alt: Bar chart: YouTube views per Angels Among Us docuseries episode, from 7.0 million for episode 1 to 1.2 million for episode 6.
blocks.caption: Angels Among Us views per episode on YouTube, collected 19 Oct 2026. Earlier episodes have had longer to accumulate views, so the decline is partly an age effect.

blocks.alt: Bar chart: median TikTok views per post by content category, posts from 24 hours before to 2 hours after go-live. Wings 3.6M (1 post), backstage 3.4M (7), docuseries 3.1M (1), casting reveal 1.5M (3), tune-in 1.4M (7), commerce 1.3M (1).
blocks.caption: Median views per post by content category, @victoriassecret TikTok, posts from 24 hours before to 2 hours after go-live (n per category in brackets). Categories with one post are shown for completeness, not as evidence.

paras: The official full-show stream had **10.3 million views 3.3 hours after going live** ([Internet Archive capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20261019020843/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zJOaqPMHs7Y)) and **20,973,365 views at 20.5 hours** ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zJOaqPMHs7Y), read 19 Oct, 20:18 BST).

To compare fairly, we read the 2025 stream’s public view counter from Internet Archive captures taken at similar points after it went live: 5.4 million at 2.8 hours ([capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20251016011035/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SdSSPF1S-Uc)), 18.1 million at 19.3 hours ([capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20251016174218/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SdSSPF1S-Uc)) and 21.3 million at 27.5 hours ([capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20251017015525/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SdSSPF1S-Uc)). Interpolating between the last two, 2026 was **about 13% ahead at the same age**. The honest range, using either bracketing capture, is −2% to +16%.

blocks.alt: Line chart: cumulative YouTube views of the official full-show livestream by hours after go-live. 2026 reaches 21.0 million at 20.5 hours; 2025 reached about 18.6 million at the same point.
blocks.caption: Cumulative views of the official full-show YouTube stream, 2025 vs 2026, by hours after go-live. Source: YouTube public counters via Internet Archive captures and a direct read on 19 Oct 2026, 20:18 BST. Views are not unique viewers.

paras: At 20 hours the 2026 stream had **651,736 likes**, against roughly 925,000 for 2025 at the same age: **0.031 likes per view, down from 0.050**. One plausible reading is a broader, more casual audience. Public data can’t confirm it.

[Google Trends](https://trends.google.com/trends/explore) lets us put the 2025 and 2026 show windows on the same scale. Despite attracting more views than in 2025, Google search interest for the show **fell by 44% worldwide** and **7% in the US**, while **rising by 12% in Great Britain**.

This divergence suggests that audience attention may increasingly be captured within social and video platforms rather than reflected in search activity. However, Google Trends measures relative search interest, not actual search volumes, and public data cannot establish the reasons behind this shift or whether increased viewership translated into purchases.

blocks.alt: Three line charts of Google search interest for victoria's secret fashion show around show day, 2025 vs 2026, for the US, Great Britain and worldwide.
blocks.caption: Google search interest for “victoria’s secret fashion show”, 2025 vs 2026 show windows. One request per region, so both years share the same 0–100 scale. Collected 19 Oct 2026, 20:31 BST; 19 Oct was a partial day.

blocks.text: Kylie got the conversation. The Angels got the views.

paras: Kylie Jenner closed the show wearing the returning **Fantasy Bra**, made with Jacob & Co. Victoria’s Secret’s own TikTok confirmed it: “@Kylie Jenner made history tonight when she walked down the runway in the Fantasy Bra.” The widely reported value of **$50 million is an estimate attributed to Vogue**, not a sale price ([Yahoo / Cover Media, 19 Oct](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/celebrity/articles/kylie-jenner-dazzles-fantasy-bra-080448156.html)). Chief creative officer Adam Selman said Jenner “extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV”, as reported from a Vogue interview ([E! News, 19 Oct](https://www.eonline.com/news/1437189/victorias-secret-defends-kylie-jenner-wearing-fantasy-bra-at-fashion-show)). Whether she was paid, or holds an ambassador role, has not been disclosed.

items: **Instagram:** same likes (about 3 million each), but Kylie’s post drew 35,000 comments to Adriana Lima’s 20,000 ([Kylie’s Reel](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeqKHJLOPxl/), [Adriana’s Reel](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeqQoHllWjL/)).

**TikTok:** her five posts from the first six hours after the show started had a median of 1.3 million views, level with the brand’s other clips from the same hours. The biggest view counts went to legacy Angels and backstage content.
**Search:** “kylie jenner” and “fantasy bra” both spiked on Google Trends the day after the show.

paras: On this evidence, **celebrity drives conversation; heritage drives reach.**

The show ran live on three free platforms and in cinemas. In the following 20 hours the brand published **15 YouTube uploads and 44 TikToks**. At least six TikToks promoted an official **“After Party LIVE on TikTok Shop”** at 8:45 PM ET, straight after the runway, and the UK site led with “Shop Fashion Show” and a limited-edition “Backstage Edit” ([victoriassecret.co.uk](https://www.victoriassecret.co.uk/), observed 19 Oct). One wings-only TikTok, “800 pounds arriving tomorrow”, drew **3.6 million views**: a reminder of how much a single distinctive brand asset can carry.

items: **Collection window:** 19 October 2026, 19:15–20:35 BST, 19.5–21 hours after go-live. Every count is a snapshot that keeps growing.
**YouTube:** 35 official videos; views, likes, comments, publish time and live start/end read from each public watch page.
**2025 benchmark:** the same fields from Internet Archive captures of the 2025 stream page.
**TikTok:** all 144 posts visible on the official profile. Each post’s creation time was decoded from its ID, so we could place it before, during or after the show.
**Instagram:** the 12 most recent posts, which is all a logged-out visitor can see.
**Google Trends:** one request per region covering both years’ windows, so 2025 and 2026 share the same 0–100 scale.

**Categorisation:** posts were hand-coded by content type (backstage, runway, performance, casting reveal, countdown, docuseries, commerce, Fantasy Bra, wings) and by talent. The coding is stored with the data so anyone can challenge it.

**Calculations:** likes per view, comments per 1,000 likes, medians alongside means, and linear interpolation for the 2025 comparison, all reproduced in a Python/pandas script against a 535-row observation table with a source URL on every row.

blocks.text: What public data can’t tell us

items: **Views are not people.** One person can watch three times on two platforms. We never add platform totals together and call it reach.

**Sales.** No sales, traffic or conversion figure has been tied to the show. Victoria’s Secret & Co. reports the quarter that includes it around December 2026, and even then quarterly revenue mixes every channel and has no counterfactual.
**Return on spend.** Production, talent and media costs aren’t public.
**Kylie’s value.** Without her terms and a brand-lift test, nobody outside the company can say how much of her buzz turned into revenue.
**Live shopping.** TikTok Shop results from the After Party aren’t public.
**2026 creator, earned-media and peak-viewer figures** hadn’t been published at the time of research.

paras: Answering these needs first-party data: daily sales by channel, site analytics by traffic source, TikTok Shop data, talent and production costs, and a holdout test or marketing-mix model.

blocks.text: Steal the system, not the budget

items: **Make the launch a series:** countdown, reveal, finale. Most of Victoria’s Secret’s best-performing content came before the show.
**Own one asset people know without your name.** A TikTok of nothing but wings drew 3.6 million views.
**Film backstage.** It often outperforms the main event.
**Plan the clips before the day.** One broadcast became 59 YouTube and TikTok entry points within 20 hours.
**Put the checkout one tap from the moment.**
**Decide what you’ll measure before you post**, or you’ll be left counting views.

blocks.text: Beautiful stops the scroll. Evidence earns the decision.

paras: Victoria’s Secret’s greatest asset isn’t lingerie. It’s anticipation: built over weeks, distributed everywhere and placed next to a shop. The public numbers show the strategy working on attention. Only first-party data can show whether it worked on revenue.
That gap is where noova works: connecting brand, creative, analytics and growth, so you know why your marketing works, not just how it looks.
